name: insimul-unreal-tooling
comment: `check` is the toolchain-free gate — a structural scan, the corpus manifest,
the band-120 mechanic host manifest (every host interface core's module
manifest names is mirrored, member for member, and implemented or stubbed with
a stated consequence), and the band-120 decision-corpus survey. The corpus
manifest carries per-area case counts AND a caseFloor that never drops on its
own (146 US-2), so a corpus that SHRINKS fails rather than re-hashing clean.
`check:mechanic-corpora` is the survey: what the DECISION-layer corpora hold,
which of them anything here can run (today: none, and it names the blocker),
and the vendored genre-activation table against MODULE_HOSTS.json. It needs no
binaries — the one fact that would, `core.methods`, is measured once by ctest
mechanic_bridge and mirrored here — and it carries eleven negative controls so
'0 of 212 executable' is a measurement rather than a decoration.
`check:packs` verifies the vendored rule PACK TEXTS — the data an exported game
consults — against Content/Data/insimul/packs/PACKS.json, and `check:activation`
(146 US-3) checks the activation DATA and SOURCES: the shipped table is the
vendored mirror byte for byte, every genre re-resolves to the packs and hosts its
own module rows name, no module id or pack area appears in an activation source,
and the sample scene's scenario is one this build could run. The two claims that
are about a KNOWLEDGE BASE — an inactive module's vocabulary being ABSENT, and the
scene's steps getting core's real answers — are ctest `activation_witness`, not a
second implementation in JavaScript.
`check:host` compiles the PORTABLE slice of the runtime
module and runs it against the golden fixtures; it needs only cmake and a C++17
compiler (no Unreal, no UBT), so the merge gate runs it too. It drops the
libinsimulcore legs with a configure-time WARNING when no native build is
beside it — read that warning rather than the pass count.
`check:host:binaries` is the same suite with -DINSIMUL_REQUIRE_BINARIES=ON, so
that warning becomes a hard failure: it is this harness's --require-binaries,
and it is what proves an adoption claim rather than assuming one. It adds the
four bridge-linked legs — radiant_bridge, quest_parity_core, mechanic_bridge
(146 US-1), which asks the shipped libinsimulcore `core.methods` and pins
the answer so a mechanic row ARRIVING fails as loudly as one disappearing, and
prolog_corpus (146 US-2), which drives all 255 vendored Prolog cases —
including the 125 band-120 mechanic-* cases — through insimul::InsimulKB, the
plugin's own libinsimul wrapper, and diffs core's golden solution sets.
`check:full` is check + check:host:binaries.

scripts.check: node verify-unreal/check.mjs && node vendor-conformance.mjs --check && node verify-mechanics/check-mechanics.mjs && node verify-mechanics/check-mechanic-corpora.mjs && node vendor-packs/vendor-packs.mjs --check && node verify-mechanics/check-activation.mjs
scripts.check:host: cmake -S verify-unreal -B verify-unreal/build && cmake --build verify-unreal/build && ctest --test-dir verify-unreal/build --output-on-failure
scripts.check:host:binaries: cmake -S verify-unreal -B verify-unreal/build -DINSIMUL_REQUIRE_BINARIES=ON && cmake --build verify-unreal/build && ctest --test-dir verify-unreal/build --output-on-failure
scripts.check:full: npm run check && npm run check:host:binaries
